facts.statement: As of access date (16-Jul-2026), no primary company press release confirming actual commissioning of the Damanjodi 5th-stream alumina refinery (+1 MTPA) was located. Instead, a related tender for 'Miscellaneous Civil, Structural and Piping works for ASSISTING the commissioning' was ePublished 24-Jun-2026 with a pre-bid meeting 01-Jul-2026 — i.e., commissioning-support works were still being tendered in late June/early July 2026, and a May-2026 site review described evaluating 'construction progress, infrastructure development, and overall project readiness' (forward-looking language, not a completion statement).

The re-guided June-2026 commissioning target for the 5th-stream refinery appears NOT to have been confirmed as achieved as of the access date; the presence of a commissioning-support tender still in pre-bid stage in early July 2026 is inconsistent with a completed June-2026 commissioning, though it does not rule out a partial/phased start. No Q1 FY2027 transcript or investor presentation (expected ~Aug-2026) was available to confirm status definitively.

Pottangi bauxite mine: NALCO's Board approved the MDO contract award to Dilip Buildcon on 9-Dec-2025 (base mining charge Rs.423/tonne, 25-year term; Phase 1 EPC ~Rs.1,750 cr covering OLCC/roads/water intake and 7 mt bauxite handling over 3 years; Phase 2 ~Rs.3,250 cr covering 77 mt bauxite over 22 years). Management (CMD) reiterated a target to start mining 'by June 2026' as of a Dec-2025 statement. No post-April-2026 press release confirming actual mining commencement was located in this pass.

GoI (President of India) shareholding: the NALCO investor-relations shareholding-pattern index page (primary source) confirms a Q1FY2027 (quarter ended 30-Jun-2026) shareholding-pattern PDF was filed and posted 09-Jul-2026 — the most recent of 41 quarterly filings 2016-2026 — but the exact promoter percentage was not extractable from the page (document index only, PDF not fetched). A secondary aggregator states promoter holding at 51.3% for the Jun-2026 quarter (FII 22%, DII 11.2%, public 15.5%), consistent with the 51.28% figure used in the original DR1 pass, but this remains a secondary/unverified-tier corroboration, not a directly-read primary PDF figure.

No OFS or disinvestment transaction for NALCO was found. The only CPSE OFS active around this period is NLC India (up to 3% stake, floor price Rs.303/share, opened 8-9 Jun-2026) — a different, unrelated CPSE. GoI unencumbered-shareholding confirmation for NALCO (President of India shares, no pledge) for FY ended 31-Mar-2026 was separately corroborated.

Board composition / independent-director vacancy CONFIRMED as an active, disclosed, and penalized compliance gap (upgrades the prior DR1 'routine tenure-expiry, governance watch item' framing to an active governance red flag). Per NALCO's own FY2026 Annual Secretarial Compliance Report (as reported by trade press): the board did not meet the SEBI LODR Regulation 17(1) requirement of >=50% independent directors during parts of FY2026, following the 31-Mar-2026 cessation of three independent directors (Trupti Kamlesh Patel, Ajay Narang, Patel Sanjaykumar) without replacements yet named. This also affected Audit Committee, Nomination & Remuneration Committee, and Stakeholders Relationship Committee composition. BSE and NSE each fined NALCO Rs.5,42,800 (total Rs.10,85,600, incl. 18% GST) via notices dated 27-Feb-2026 for the Q3FY26 (quarter ended 31-Dec-2025) non-compliance. NALCO requested a fine waiver (letter dated 17-Mar-2026) citing that ID appointments are controlled by the President of India/Administrative Ministry, outside company control; waiver outcome not yet reported as of access date.

CBI opened a probe (2026) into recruitment-fraud allegations at NALCO's Bhubaneswar office/Haradghana site — complaints alleged ~20 people were promised/given jobs without an official advertisement. NALCO's public response states the CBI visit was a routine verification of an unverified external complaint (no raid, no document seizure), and that press characterization as a 'raid' is misleading. This reads as an external recruitment-fraud/impersonation-scheme complaint under CBI review, not a confirmed adverse finding against NALCO management or an admission of wrongdoing by the company; status of the CBI inquiry (ongoing/closed) not confirmed in this pass.

No SEBI enforcement order, NCLT/NCLAT case, or IBBI proceeding specifically naming NALCO or its current directors was located via general web search in this pass. This remains an absence-of-evidence result, not a certified docket-level clean scan: SEBI's enforcement-order search and NCLT/NCLAT case-search portals require interactive form submission (case number/party name lookup) that is not indexable by search engines and was not directly queried via fetch in this pass.

No NALCO-specific CAG Section 143(6) supplementary-audit para for FY2023-FY2025 was located. The only NALCO-specific CAG finding surfaced (already logged in original DR1 pass) is a Performance Audit covering FY2012-13 to FY2016-17 (production-inefficiency, ~Rs.1,086.63 cr foregone contribution from a smelter power shortfall) — outside the FY2023-FY2025 window and an operational, not accounting/fraud, finding. A CAG 'Report No. 18 of 2025, Union Government (Commercial)' exists in CAG's report list but its PDF content (and whether it references NALCO) was not fetched/confirmed in this pass. This remains an unresolved absence-of-evidence result, consistent with the company's own claim of a clean CAG history but not independently verified against the primary CAG document.

FY2026 (year ended 31-Mar-2026) audited consolidated results confirmed: PAT Rs.5,815.76 cr, revenue from operations Rs.17,843.05 cr, total income Rs.18,508.88 cr, cumulative FY26 dividend Rs.10.50/share (3rd interim Rs.2/share), Q4 standalone PAT Rs.1,718 cr — materially matching the Q4 PPT figures used in the fundamental-analyst's original pass (revenue 17,843 cr, PAT 5,816 cr rounding). No FY26 year-end cash/investment balance-sheet figure was found in press coverage of the results; the only cash figures located (Rs.7,586.55 cr per one source, ~Rs.7,900 cr per another) are explicitly H1FY26/interim-period figures, not the FY26 year-end closing balance, so management's Rs.20,000 cr+ FY26 year-end cash/investments projection could not be directly corroborated or refuted from external sources in this pass.
